substeps.caption: The lab's LECO PX500, refitted for the arm: a magnetic platen, and six steel discs in a magazine, each pre-loaded with its paper or cloth under its own retaining ring.
The head lifts clear (our extra lift). The arm changes disc, paper and ring as one piece, by the handle on the ring.
320 grit: out of the magazine and onto the magnetic platen, which holds the steel disc flat.
Head down, water on: the lab's SOP (PR #258), its gentle settings 35, 30, 150, 30 s.
Head up. The 320 disc goes back to its shelf and the 400 comes out: no paper peeled, no ring pried off.
400 grit, then 600, 800 and 1200 the same way (30 s each), rinsed between grits.
The cloth disc for the final polish, 1 um alumina from a dispenser: force 3-5, 150 rpm, 3 min.
Head down, suspension on, no water (the SOP, step 5).

Done. A person re-papers the five SiC discs between batches, off the machine: one fresh paper per grit per holder load (Buehler's note for its fully automatic VANGUARD: change SiC paper after each holder).
